title: Abraham and Isaac
summary: Abraham learned that God could be trusted with what was most precious. God provides and calls His people to trust Him deeply. When obeying God feels costly, this story reminds kids that God provides and that faith is more than words.

read_it.prompt: Read Genesis 22:1-19 like a scene you could retell: who is there, what happens, and what changes?

tell_it: Abraham learned that God could be trusted with what was most precious. Abraham obeyed God during a very hard test. God stopped him and provided a ram instead. The pressure in the scene helps the lesson feel real.
understand_it: Abraham and Isaac should not be flattened into a slogan. God provides and calls His people to trust Him deeply. When obeying God feels costly, this story reminds kids that God provides and that faith is more than words.
age_5_7_explanation: Abraham learned that God could be trusted with what was most precious.
age_8_11_explanation: Abraham obeyed God during a very hard test. God stopped him and provided a ram instead. Kids can practice retelling it with the beginning, hard moment, and God-centered ending.
teen_explanation: God provides and calls His people to trust Him deeply. A teen discussion can press into why the story mattered then and how the same truth can reshape choices now.
key_truths: God provides and calls His people to trust Him deeply.
Abraham and Isaac shows trust through a real Bible moment, not a slogan.
When obeying God feels costly, this story reminds kids that God provides and that faith is more than words.
life_application: When obeying God feels costly, this story reminds kids that God provides and that faith is more than words.

quiz_questions.question: Which answer keeps Abraham and Isaac connected to the actual passage?
quiz_questions.explanation: A ram is the story detail to remember. The bigger lesson grows out of that detail instead of floating away from the passage.

quiz_questions.question: Abraham and Isaac is mainly about trust without ignoring the actual Bible story.
quiz_questions.explanation: The theme matters because it grows out of Genesis 22:1-19, not from a random moral pasted onto the end.

memory_verse.prompt: Read Genesis 22:14 again after the lesson and connect it to the story's main choice or promise.

discussion_questions: Who needed help, courage, correction, or mercy in Abraham and Isaac?
What truth should a kid remember after reading Abraham and Isaac?
How can the group pray about Abraham and Isaac without using pretend-perfect answers?

activity.title: Provision Mountain
activity.instructions: Draw a mountain path and place a reminder at the top: God provided the ram.

prayer_prompt: Lord, use Abraham and Isaac to teach my heart, not just my memory. Help me take one faithful next step after reading Abraham and Isaac.
